chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Falling heels versus stomping heels
summary: They discuss how coming down on the heel as foot drum rested the dancer and differs from stabbing the heel.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: It was more restful to the tap dancer, because by them coming down from their toes or the ball of the foot onto the heel, it was just like he was standing up, see. And therefore, it was restful.
That's the point, I think, we were trying to get over. It's that much more progressive, because we're coming down from just using the ball of the foot to using the whole of the foot.
Which people even now find very difficult, to use heel and toe beats.
See, there's a difference in a falling heel and what you call a stomping heel. See. If you stab the heel, it's different.
It gives out a different sound?
Yeah. The stomping of the heel -- the heel is more like what they call the foot drum to a tap dancer, you see. But he was using both of the heels. Therefore that caused what he called a cramp.
